title: First Template - Basic Data-Driven Test
description: Create your first test template using [Template] tag to run the same keyword with multiple data sets.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "We need to verify power levels for 5 different systems. Instead of writing 5 separate test cases, use a template. One test, five data rows."
story.context: Templates execute the same keyword multiple times with different arguments. Each data row becomes one test execution.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Perfect! You ran 'Should Be True' five times with different conditions—one template, five executions. That's data-driven testing."

instructions: Provide 5 data rows (no keyword names, just arguments):
Each row runs Should Be True with that condition
hints: [Template] goes right after test case name

Each row executes the template keyword

theory.title: Exercise 2.3.1: Test Templates - Data-Driven Testing
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "Imagine checking 100 systems with the same validation logic. Without templates, you'd copy-paste 100 test cases. With templates, you write the test ONCE and provide 100 data rows. That's the power of data-driven testing."

Test Templates

A test template executes the same keyword repeatedly with different arguments:

*** Test Cases ***
Validation Test
    [Template]    Keyword Name
    arg1    arg2    # First execution
    arg3    arg4    # Second execution
    arg5    arg6    # Third execution

How It Works:

  • [Template] tag specifies which keyword to run
  • Each subsequent line provides arguments for one execution
  • No keyword names on data rows—just arguments
  • Each row = one test execution
  • Perfect for repetitive validations with different data

Example: Multiple Assertions

*** Test Cases ***
System Status Check
    [Template]    Should Be Equal
    Navigation      OK
    Power          OK
    Life Support   OK
    Engines        OK

Execution:

  • Should Be Equal Navigation OK
  • Should Be Equal Power OK
  • Should Be Equal Life Support OK
  • Should Be Equal Engines OK

Four executions of the same assertion, four different systems.

⚠️ Template Rules

  • [Template] must be indented (same level as keywords)
  • Data rows contain ONLY arguments (no keyword name)
  • Each row must match keyword's argument count
  • Template runs each row as separate execution
  • If one row fails, others still execute
  • Great for: validations, data verification, batch operations
